device.family: M3503 (chips/m3503.py: the M36xx family with the chip ID 0x3503, the XIP bootloader's cache-as-RAM stack and the chip's internal demodulator)

image.layout: the ALi NCRC chunk chain, bootloader chunk at 0 (next chunk at 0x06EE00)

source.note: Not recorded: added to this repository on 2026-01-20 under dumps/other with the file name it came with, which says what it is (read from a working unit, "OK")

simulator.note: As the M3503 family (2026-10-13; its bootloader, "3510-r1362", is the Globo HD-XS2's XIP kind, and its set-up code branches on the chip IDs 0x3503 and 0x3821; 0x3510 appears nowhere in it): the bootloader runs from the flash window with its stack in the cache-as-RAM lines -- as the M3801 default it popped a return address of 0xFFFFFFFF and ended at PC 0 -- and starts the application at ~34 M instructions (single-CPU, no SEE program; a silent build, two 0x01 bytes to the UART).  The application draws its "Quick Setup" menu (Menu Language English, First Audio, Second Audio, LNB Power On, Single Search, Multi Satellite Search, Main Menu) through the GE by ~100 M (14 commands; run_dump_esr250_capture_screen.py, which also presses DOWN).  A task of it hid the OSD layer (0xB8006300 bit 0) as long as the NIM device's chip ID was not an S3501's: the chip's internal demodulator, whose registers the CPU reads at 0xB8028000 + the register number, answers it (chips/m3503.py InternalDemod).  Its remote takes standard NEC frames whose key-table code keeps the frame's first address byte (ir_remote coding "necfirst": its key conversion at 0x8009C058 keeps (code >> 24) << 8 | (code & 0xFF), the older SDKs code >> 16): DOWN moves the highlight from Menu Language to First Audio.  Its key table also holds the front panel's keys (type 2, codes 0xFFxx: MENU, LEFT, RIGHT, OK, DOWN, UP), whose panel is not modelled.

desc: Its application names a satellite front end (NIM_S3501 / S3503 tuner-demodulator drivers, "Tuner 1 has no satellite select!").
